answer: A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Policies are written in karst, settled in orchard, and garden lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 33% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. That bill is paid per identity, so 306 aliases cost 44 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
